A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QT-DoG and EoQ. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DomainBed experiments, quantization ablations, flatness measurements, training trajectories, and GradCAM analyses, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds WILDS and CLIP evaluations, configuration ablations, and measurements of quantization-noise distributions.

M1.justification: The proposed weight-quantization procedure, integration with ERM, and EoQ prediction aggregation remain unchanged. The ensemble initialization clarification and additional evaluations do not establish a revised algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on the WILDS Amazon and Camelyon datasets (Section 4.1.4, Table 3), extending coverage beyond the five retained DomainBed datasets and explicitly including text inputs. WILDS was only cited in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated CLIPood comparator alongside ERM in the CLIP-based comparison (Table 6). CLIPood was cited but not evaluated in v1. Comparator membership in the retained DomainBed, quantization-method, and appendix comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce Amazon 10th-percentile accuracy, Camelyon average accuracy, a BERT model, and CLIP ViT-B/16 settings. New controlled experiments vary scaling granularity, quantization timing, and uniform-noise amplitude. Existing DomainBed splits, training budgets, and model-selection procedures are retained in Appendix B.

E4.justification: Appendices H–J add PACS ablations testing channelwise versus layerwise scaling, quantization at 1000–4000 steps, and uniform weight-noise amplitudes. Section 3.2 and Appendix L add weight-distribution, symmetry, and quantization-error analyses. Earlier flatness, bit-precision, and GradCAM analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 3.6 newly states that ensemble members are trained independently from initialization using random seeds. Both versions retain the stated three-trial standard-error reporting and omission of ensemble confidence intervals. No increase in repetitions or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values are retained, including Table 1 averages of 66.2 for QT-DoG and 68.4 for EoQ. New Table 3 reports QT-DoG versus ERM OOD scores of 55.9 versus 53.8 on Amazon and 78.4 versus 70.3 on Camelyon. Table 6 adds CLIP averages of 70.6 for QT-DoG and 70.3 for CLIPood. New ablation and noise-distribution findings substantially expand the reported results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix L introduce assumptions and an approximate derivation for uniformly distributed quantization error, using small quantization bins, smooth symmetric weight distributions, and piecewise-linear density approximations. The existing quantization equations, Taylor expansion, flatness expression, and ensemble equation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central generalization, flatness, and efficient-ensembling claims remain. However, v1's claim to demonstrate the effect theoretically and empirically becomes an empirical demonstration supported by analytical insights in v2's contributions and conclusion, narrowing the claimed strength of the theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that flatter minima do not universally imply better domain generalization, explains aggressive quantization through over-regularization, and distinguishes structured quantization noise from random uniform perturbations. The original limitations concerning ensemble training cost and bit-width selection are retained in Appendix C.

D1.justification: v2's abstract announces released code and supplies a project link, replacing v1's future-release promise, although Appendix M retains future-tense wording. v2 also documents additional model configurations and ablation settings and changes the reported CUDA version from 11.1 to 12.1. Most original implementation details are relocated unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds quantization-noise references such as Gray and Neuhoff and Boncelet, qualifies the flatness discussion using Andriushchenko and Mueller, and adds recent quantization and CLIP-related works. These refine the supporting literature and positioning without replacing the paper's central novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: dataset descriptions, implementation details, and limitations move from the main text to Appendices A–C; experimental subsections are reordered; and the appendix structure expands around new analyses. Contributions and analytical explanations are revised, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper, with extensive resizing and relocation of existing displays. v2 adds Tables 3, 6, and 13–15 and distribution Figures 2 and 8. The vision-transformer table drops its redundant backbone column. Existing GradCAM images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for the paper's generality and mechanism claims. WILDS, text, and CLIP evaluations extend evidence beyond v1's DomainBed image settings, while Appendices H–J directly test previously unexamined scaling, timing, and generic-noise explanations. More cautious theoretical framing also improves claim calibration. The added protocols remain tersely documented, the uniform-noise argument is approximate, and code-release wording is inconsistent, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
